title: Conditions for non-soficity of a $\mathbb{Z}^2$-subshift
speaker: Ilkka Törmä
abstract: We survey some known conditions for non-soficity of $\mathbb{Z}^2$-subshifts, in particular exchange arguments, subsystem entropy and Kolmogorov-complexity.

title: $BS(1,2) \not\hookrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}(X)$
speaker: Ville Salo
abstract: We prove the result of Cyr-Franks-Kra-Petite showing that the metabelian Baumslag-Solitar group BS(1, 2) does not embed in the automorphism group of a zero-entropy subshift X.

title: De Rham's theorem
speaker: Lumi Miinalainen
abstract: Smooth manifolds are an important class of topological spaces, enabling the use of tools from analysis via a local coordinate structure. De Rham's theorem uncovers a deep connection between the analytical and topological properties of such a space: the de Rham cohomology of a smooth manifold, defined using the differentiable structure, in fact coincides with the singular cohomology arising from just continuous maps. Moreover, this isomorphism is given by integration. The theorem also admits a wide generalisation in terms of sheaf cohomology. This talk, based on my Master's Thesis work at the University of Helsinki, discusses primarily the classical formulation of the theorem.

title: Linearly recurrent shifts have small automorphism groups
speaker: Ilkka Törmä

title: Asymptotic nilpotency implies nilpotency on $A^{\mathbb{Z}}$
speaker: Ville Salo
abstract: We give the argument of Richard and Guillon showing that if a cellular automaton has the property that every initial configuration converges to the zero point under the time evolution, then actually the cellular automaton is a root of the zero map.
